title: plasma-nm fails to read a SAML cookie for a GlobalProtect VPN, then crashes in QWidgetPrivate::windowHandle()
line: Cancelling a passkey prompt during an OpenConnect/GlobalProtect SAML login no longer crashes the network service when the login page asks again.
explanation: The OpenConnect auth widget opens a WebAuth (passkey) dialog with WA_DeleteOnClose and keeps a raw pointer to it. When the request is cancelled or completed the dialog closes and deletes itself, but the pointer is never cleared, so when the SAML page reloads and asks for a passkey again, handleWebAuthUxRequested() calls close() on the freed dialog and kded6 segfaults (the reporter's backtrace). The pointer is now a QPointer, which becomes null when the dialog is deleted, and the update branch checks it too.

commits.message:
openconnect: don't close a WebAuth dialog that was already deleted

The WebAuth dialog deletes itself when closed, but the pointer to it
was kept, so the next passkey request after the login page reloaded
called close() on freed memory and crashed kded. Track it with QPointer.

BUG: 515706

media.caption: Master: SAML login page asks for a passkey, WebAuth dialog open
Master: after Cancel the page reloads, asks again and kded6 crashes; the VPN dialog is gone
Master: Connect, passkey prompt, Cancel, crash
Fix: after Cancel the page reloads and a fresh passkey prompt opens, kded6 keeps running
Fix: two Cancel/reload cycles, then the VPN dialog is cancelled normally

review.text: Textbook dangling-pointer fix: the WA_DeleteOnClose dialog was tracked with a raw pointer that was never cleared, and the crash in the backtrace is exactly the close() on it. Switching to QPointer (already included) and guarding the updateDisplay() branch is the minimal, idiomatic Qt fix. The fake SAML gateway repro shows the crash before and repeated Cancel/reload cycles surviving after.
